chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

“If a boy steals, he is pardoned; if he repeats it, he is disciplined; if he repeats it, the tips of the fingers are cut off; if he repeats it, lower than that is cut.” And he said: “ʿAlī عليه السلام was brought a غلام whose having experienced ihtilām was doubtful, so he cut off the tips of the fingers.”

key_terms.أَطْرَافُ ٱلْأَصَابِعِ: the ends or tips of the fingers
key_terms.عُزِّرَ: was subjected to discretionary disciplinary punishment
key_terms.عُفِيَ: was pardoned and excused from punishment
key_terms.ٱحْتِلَامِهِ: his experiencing a nocturnal emission, a sign of puberty
key_terms.ٱلصَّبِيُّ: a minor boy not fully legally accountable

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on repeated theft by a minor?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling regarding theft committed by a minor, outlining a graduated response beginning with pardon and then escalating punishment upon repeated offense. It also cites a case of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning a youth whose puberty was uncertain, in which the tips of the fingers were cut off.
